## 1. Should the Mountain View City Council proceed with the second phase of protected bike lanes on El Camino Real, which would remove 62 on-street parking spaces between Castro Street and Grant Road?

*mountain view, ca · generated by the agent (7 model calls, $0.0) · id `fbaec2d6322a`*

- Article: [Mountain View council to vote on removing 62 parking spaces for El Camino bike lanes](file://eval/articles/demo_bike_lane.txt)

**Options** (0 votes):

- Yes, proceed with the bike lanes as planned
- Yes, but only if the project includes a comprehensive parking study first
- No, delay or reconsider the bike lanes
- Not sure / need more information

**The case for:** Supporters say the first phase of the bike lanes reduced bike-involved collisions by 31% and that the project is critical for improving safety for cyclists. The project is also supported by the Mountain View Bicycle Coalition. The city has received a regional transportation grant that would cover $2.9 million of the $4.2 million cost, but the grant expires if construction does not begin by spring.

**The case against:** Opponents argue that the removal of parking spaces could harm local businesses, as customers may drive less if they cannot park. A group of business owners has petitioned the council to conduct a parking study first. Some residents suggest a compromise that would keep parking on one side of the street and narrow the bike lane buffer.

**Who can vote:** ZIPs 94040, 94041, 94043, 94035, 94039, 94042 · **Decision date:** 2026-09-29

**Critic:** 1 pass(es), final draft accepted

## 2. As San Jose drafts new data center standards for a City Council vote in December, which approach should the city take?

*san jose, ca · hand-seeded for the demo · id `seed-sj-data-centers`*

- Article: [San Jose mayor meets with neighbors complaining about data center noise](https://www.newsbreak.com/news/4893256207854-san-jose-mayor-meets-with-neighbors-complaining-about-data-center-noise)

**Options** (12 votes, simulated):

- Adopt binding noise, light and recycled-water requirements — 6 (50%)
- Pause new data centers until standards are adopted — 1 (8%)
- Work with operators voluntarily rather than new rules — 5 (42%)
- Not sure / need more information — 0 (0%)

**The case for:** South San Jose residents near Great Oaks Boulevard describe a constant hum and bright lights from nearby data centers, and Mayor Mahan says the city should require data centers to connect to and pay for the recycled-water network, which would also help expand that system.

**The case against:** The residents themselves say they are not against data centers, only the noise and lights; the mayor's first step is to ask operators to add fan shielding and dim lights, and the city has not followed other cities that imposed moratoriums.

**Who can vote:** ZIPs 95110, 95111, 95112, 95113, 95116, 95117, 95118, 95120, 95121, 95122, 95123, 95124, 95125, 95126, 95127, 95128, 95129, 95130, 95131, 95132, 95133, 95134, 95135, 95136, 95138, 95139, 95148

**Sources:** https://www.newsbreak.com/news/4893256207854-san-jose-mayor-meets-with-neighbors-complaining-about-data-center-noise

## 3. Should the San Jose City Council adopt the proposed self-checkout rules for grocery stores and pharmacies, including a 15-item limit, at least one staffed lane, and one employee for every three kiosks?

*san jose, ca · hand-seeded for the demo · id `seed-sj-self-checkout`*

- Article: [San Jose could be first Bay Area city to introduce self-checkout line regulations](https://www.newsbreak.com/news/4892773502565-san-jose-could-be-first-bay-area-city-to-introduce-self-checkout-line-regulations)

**Options** (302 votes, simulated):

- Yes, adopt the rules as proposed — 116 (38%)
- Yes, but only the staffed-lane requirement — 77 (25%)
- No, leave self-checkout decisions to stores — 81 (27%)
- Not sure / need more information — 28 (9%)

**The case for:** Councilmembers Candelas and Cohen, backed by the UFCW Local 5 union, say the rules protect workers who now juggle several kiosks plus theft prevention, help seniors who struggle with the technology, and address retail theft that city officials say costs up to $400,000 a year in sales tax.

**The case against:** The California Grocers Association says the rules would raise grocery prices, create longer lines, and put workers in danger without stopping crime. Only a few Southern California cities have adopted similar limits so far.

**Who can vote:** ZIPs 95110, 95111, 95112, 95113, 95116, 95117, 95118, 95120, 95121, 95122, 95123, 95124, 95125, 95126, 95127, 95128, 95129, 95130, 95131, 95132, 95133, 95134, 95135, 95136, 95138, 95139, 95148

**Sources:** https://www.newsbreak.com/news/4892773502565-san-jose-could-be-first-bay-area-city-to-introduce-self-checkout-line-regulations

## 4. Should the Mountain View Whisman School District buy the 1.8-acre parcel under its 144-unit staff housing on Shoreline Boulevard rather than lease it for $1.9 million a year?

*mountain view, ca · hand-seeded for the demo · id `seed-teacher-housing-land`*

- Article: [Mountain View Whisman looks to buy the land teacher housing is built on](https://www.newsbreak.com/news/3770002815473-mountain-view-whisman-looks-to-buy-the-land-teacher-housing-is-built-on)

**Options** (58 votes, simulated):

- Yes, buy the land — 25 (43%)
- Yes, but only if the price is below the long-term lease cost — 24 (41%)
- No, keep leasing — 7 (12%)
- Not sure / need more information — 2 (3%)

**The case for:** The district says owning the land would eliminate a $1.9 million annual ground lease and help it keep rents cost-neutral for teachers and staff who struggle with regional housing costs. The board is voting on an option agreement that only gives it the right to buy by June 30.

**The case against:** The purchase price is not yet known and depends on negotiations with the developer; the district has already spent about $88 million in Measure T bond money on the building, and the lease talks have so far taken place in closed session.

**Who can vote:** ZIPs 94040, 94041, 94043, 94035, 94039, 94042 · **Decision date:** 2025-01-23

**Sources:** https://www.newsbreak.com/news/3770002815473-mountain-view-whisman-looks-to-buy-the-land-teacher-housing-is-built-on

## 5. Should the Mountain View City Council eliminate minimum parking requirements for new residential projects in the Downtown, San Antonio, East Whisman and El Camino Real plan areas?

*mountain view, ca · hand-seeded for the demo · id `seed-parking-minimums`*

- Article: [Mountain View looks to eliminate parking requirements for housing in parts of the city](https://www.newsbreak.com/news/3606213450231-mountain-view-looks-to-eliminate-parking-requirements-for-housing-in-parts-of-the-city)

**Options** (143 votes, simulated):

- Yes, eliminate them as recommended — 30 (21%)
- Yes, but keep minimums for accessible and EV parking — 66 (46%)
- No, keep the current requirements — 38 (27%)
- Not sure / need more information — 9 (6%)

**The case for:** City planners say removing minimums gives developers flexibility for more diverse housing and mixed-use projects. The change is called for in the city's housing element and follows state law AB 2097, and the Environmental Planning Commission recommended it on a 4-0-1 vote.

**The case against:** Commissioners who voted for the recommendation still raised concerns: with no minimum, a project could omit accessible and EV parking entirely, one commissioner said the policy could keep disabled residents from living or working here, and another noted transit ridership has not recovered since the pandemic.

**Who can vote:** ZIPs 94040, 94041, 94043, 94035, 94039, 94042

**Sources:** https://www.newsbreak.com/news/3606213450231-mountain-view-looks-to-eliminate-parking-requirements-for-housing-in-parts-of-the-city

## 6. Should the Mountain View City Council approve CRP Affordable's eight-story, 100-unit affordable apartment building at 334 San Antonio Road with 16 parking spaces?

*mountain view, ca · hand-seeded for the demo · id `seed-san-antonio-100`*

- Article: [Mountain View Planning Commission backs affordable housing development with little parking](https://www.newsbreak.com/san-jos-spotlight-510761/3702094647051-mountain-view-planning-commission-backs-affordable-housing-development-with-little-parking)

**Options** (214 votes, simulated):

- Yes, approve as proposed — 103 (48%)
- Yes, but require more parking — 55 (26%)
- No, do not approve — 38 (18%)
- Not sure / need more information — 18 (8%)

**The case for:** The Environmental Planning Commission unanimously supported the project, citing its affordability (households at or below 80% of area median income) and its family-sized units. The developer says the site is within half a mile of transit, affordable tenants tend to own fewer cars, and it will add 100 bicycle spaces and a three-year $50 transit subsidy.

**The case against:** Several commissioners said 16 spaces is unreasonably low for 100 units, compared with a typical ratio of 0.41 to 0.75 spaces per unit cited by the city's housing director, and questioned whether San Antonio Road has usable bus service for residents to rely on.

**Who can vote:** ZIPs 94040, 94041, 94043, 94035, 94039, 94042

**Sources:** https://www.newsbreak.com/san-jos-spotlight-510761/3702094647051-mountain-view-planning-commission-backs-affordable-housing-development-with-little-parking
